corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 61, choose only after measuring the deployed alternatives; the source provides no platform facts that justify a priori selection. Assumptions to declare are the model/checkpoint and precision, GPU count/type and usable memory, interconnect topology and placement, software/runtime versions, request prompt/output-length distribution, offered load and concurrency, batching/scheduler policy, power limits, warm-up and compilation state, and the latency SLA (p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, TTFT, and TPOT, all in ms). Also define throughput (requests/s or tokens/s), quality/error gates, availability target, whether reconfiguration is permitted, and what failure budget applies. Treat these as controlled inputs or estimates until measured; do not invent hardware or latency values.

Pre-register a falsifiable hypothesis with a numerical margin, for example: at a named offered load and fixed quality, memory, error, and availability gates, the selected feasible strategy will lower p99 end-to-end latency by at least M ms (or M%) versus the other strategy. Enumerate feasible tensor-parallel degrees and pipeline layer partitions, including stage balance, activation memory, batch size, and microbatch count. Use randomized, interleaved paired trials on the same hashed request set, identical software and placement, equal warm-up/compilation, and a declared sample size, exclusions, stopping rule, and uncertainty method. Keep tuning/calibration requests disjoint from the held-out evaluation set.

Measure per-GPU memory headroom/utilization, achieved throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT/TPOT, tensor communication bytes and time, synchronization waits, pipeline bubbles, stage queueing, load imbalance, host/device transfers, and energy if relevant. Report units, sample counts, confidence intervals, and raw per-request data. Gate a choice on both the latency hypothesis and quality, correctness, memory, error, and availability results. Stratify or randomize prompt/output lengths, concurrency, topology, thermal state, background load, cache state, and scheduler effects; check that instrumentation overhead and warm-up do not explain the result.

Before rollout, define failure handling: inject representative GPU/link/worker failures in a staging environment, measure detection, draining, restart, state recovery, degraded-mode latency, and reconfiguration time, and document data-loss and retry behavior. Use least-privilege access, redact request content, isolate experiments from production, and retain only authorized telemetry. Start with a reversible canary, a versioned configuration, health and latency/error thresholds, an owner, and an automatic rollback trigger. Roll back on threshold breach, quality regression, unsafe error/availability behavior, unrecoverable worker loss, or failure to reproduce the held-out result. The result remains provisional until hardware inventory, preregistered plan, raw telemetry, quality/availability data, recovery logs, and independent domain-expert review are available.
